contributions: Formal taxonomy of multi-hop and conjunctive queries (EPFO class including 1p, 2p, 3p, 2i, 3i, pi, ip query types)
Query2Box model: geometric box embeddings for representing queries as hyper-rectangles with projection (relation traversal) and intersection (logical AND) operators

Neural Bellman-Ford Network (NBFNet): a GNN that generalizes the Bellman-Ford shortest-path algorithm with query-conditioned initialization and relation-modulated message passing for multi-hop path reasoning
limitations: Query2Box cannot represent disjunction (OR) cleanly since the union of two boxes is not a box; it approximates OR by taking maximum scores across disjuncts, which is non-differentiable at query boundaries
Query2Box cannot handle negation (NOT) because the complement of a hyper-rectangle is a non-convex union of 2d half-spaces with no compact box representation
Pure graph traversal fails on incomplete KGs due to exponential recall degradation with path length
NBFNet is computationally more expensive than Query2Box on dense KGs
methods: The chapter develops two embedding-based approaches for multi-hop KG query answering. Query2Box (Ren et al., 2020) represents each query as an axis-aligned hyper-rectangle defined by a center and offset vector; relation projection shifts the center and expands the offset via learned parameters with softplus, while logical conjunction is handled by attention-weighted center averaging and sigmoid-shrunk offset intersection. NBFNet (Zhu et al., 2021) generalizes the Bellman-Ford algorithm by replacing scalar distances with representation vectors, using a DistMult-inspired query-conditioned message function h_u ⊙ (W_r' r_q), and initializing only the source entity with the query relation embedding so that information propagates conditionally from the query.
results: On an 80% complete KG, pure graph traversal recall drops exponentially: 64% at 2 hops, 51% at 3 hops, and 33% at 5 hops. For biomedical KGs that are only 30-50% complete, the situation is far worse. Query2Box inference cost is O(|E|) per query after O(L) query construction time, enabling real-time QA on KGs with 1 million entities in milliseconds on GPU. NBFNet has O(|T| * T) per query cost, making it cheaper on sparse KGs but more expensive on dense ones compared to Query2Box's O(|E| * d).
tldr: This chapter extends knowledge graph embeddings from single-triple completion to multi-hop and conjunctive query answering, presenting two approaches: Query2Box, which represents queries as geometric boxes for efficient conjunctive query evaluation, and Neural Bellman-Ford Networks, which generalize the shortest-path algorithm to learn query-conditioned reachability through graph structure.
